title: JuICE: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Judge in Identifying Cultural Errors
abstract: arXiv:2605.26955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed to users around the world, they are integrated into everyday tasks across diverse cultural contexts, from drafting personal communications to brainstorming creative ideas. These tasks are inherently cultural: they require contextual appropriateness, symbolic resonance, and tacit cultural expectations that native speakers draw on instinctively, meaning that a response can be factually plausible yet unmistakably wrong to a local reader. Existing cultural benchmarks have treated culture as a flat set of facts via fact verification or norm entailment methods, and have adopted LLM-as-a-Judge without examining whether they can capture such thick cultural errors. To address this gap, we present JuICE (Benchmark for LLM-Judge in Identifying Cultural Errors), a multilingual dataset of 7,470 span-level annotations of cultural and linguistic errors in long-form LLM responses. translated_title: JuICE：用于评估LLM裁判识别文化错误能力的基准
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地部署给全球用户，它们被集成到跨多种文化背景的日常任务中，从起草个人通信到头脑风暴创意想法。这些任务本质上具有文化属性：它们需要上下文的恰当性、符号的共鸣以及母语使用者凭本能运用的隐性文化期望，这意味着一个回复可能在事实上看似合理，但对当地读者而言却明显是错误的。现有的文化基准通过事实验证或规范蕴含方法将文化视为一组扁平的事实，并且在采用“LLM作为裁判”（LLM-as-a-Judge）时，并未检验其是否能够捕捉此类深层次的文化错误。为弥补这一空白，我们提出了JuICE（LLM裁判识别文化错误能力评估基准），这是一个多语言数据集，包含对长篇LLM回复中文化和语言错误的7,470个片段级标注。
tldr: JuICE是一个包含7,470个片段级标注的多语言基准数据集，用于评估LLM裁判识别长篇回复中深层文化错误的能力，弥补了现有文化基准将文化简化为扁平事实集合的不足。
